\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Concentration}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Applications.KKL.Concentration
\section{Overview}
The low degree Fourier mass involving omitted coordinates is controlled by their influence threshold. The estimate permits endpoint noise rates and zero thresholds.

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p264-b003}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be $\pm1$-valued, let
$J\subseteq[n]$, and let $k\in\mathbb N$ and $\rho,\tau\in\mathbb R$ satisfy
$0\le\rho\le1$ and $\tau\ge0$. If every coordinate $i\notin J$ has influence at most
$\tau$, then $\rho^k\sum_{\substack{S\subseteq[n]\\|S|\le k,\ S\nsubseteq J}}\widehat
f(S)^2\le\tau^{(1-\rho)/(1+\rho)} I[f]$, where $I[f]$ is the total influence of $f$.
\end{lemma}
